newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN REJECTS ALL BIDS IN 1-YR BOND AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN REJECTS ALL BIDS IN 1-YR BOND AUCTION.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry on Tuesday rejected all 540 million crowns worth of bids in an auction of one-year state bonds, the central bank said in a statement.
The statement did not give further details and ministry officials were not immediately available for comment on the auction result.
The bonds on offered had a fixed annual coupon of 10.00 percent. The ministry does not set minimum or maximum limit prices on submitted bids in auctions of state securities.
Average yield in the last successful auction of one-year state bonds on May 27 rose to 15.868 percent from 14.88 percent in the previous auction of similar bonds on March 25.
Local banks have been demanding high yields in state securities auctions due to an accute liquidity shortage on the local money market which has boosted short-term rates to around 26 percent.

The Finance Ministry uses T-bills and state bonds as its main tolls to cover state budget deficit, which totalled 4.692 billion crowns in the first four months of this year, up from 3.450 billion crowns in the first quarter of 1997.
